claim: Maximal PTP opening responses are obtained with 30 μM free Ca in less than 10 s.
source: Under the conditions of those experiments, the rate at which PTPs open increases over the Ca concentration range of 10–500 μM, but maximal responses are still obtained with 30 μM free Ca in less than 10 s.
evidence: This refers to original descriptions of PTP openings cited earlier (Haworth and Hunter, 1979).

claim: It is very likely that full PTP pore openings occur during the Standard MEND experiments.
source: Therefore, it is very likely that full PTP pore openings occur during these experiments.
evidence: This is inferred from the Ca concentrations achieved and the known Ca sensitivity of PTPs.

claim: PTPs are formed by dimers of the ATP synthetase.
source: In fact, more specific explanations may emerge because recent work indicates that PTPS are formed by dimers of the target of oligomycin, the ATP synthetase (Giorgio et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Giorgio et al., 2013.
